# Alma

Knowledge base for AI agents in the tools you already use. Model-agnostic framework to compound AI context and keep it up to date.

The name comes from almanac, the book navigators kept, and from the Latin and Spanish word for soul.

Built and used daily by one PM running a team of AI agents.

Site: https://alma.suvorav.com
The site is private. It is not linked from suvorav.com, it sends noindex, and it is meant to sit behind basic auth.

Install: https://github.com/ohsuvorav/alma-brain/blob/main/INSTALL.md
Prompt to paste into a coding agent: Install Alma by following https://github.com/ohsuvorav/alma-brain/blob/main/INSTALL.md

Code: https://github.com/ohsuvorav/alma-brain
The repository is not public yet.

License: MIT. Alma is free.

Author: Oleg Suvorov — https://suvorav.com

## What it is

Knowledge base for AI agents in the tools you already use. A model-agnostic framework to compound AI context and keep it up to date.

Your notes go in. Alma keeps a memory agents can search and keep up to date. The first answer comes from your own notes, with a link to the source. There is no sample brain to click through.

## What makes Alma different

Plain files any agent can read. Alma is a folder of markdown and instructions. Claude, Codex, Cursor or any provider reads the same files; switch models, keep the context. For anyone using more than one AI tool.

A wiki that writes itself. Inspired by Karpathy's LLM wiki: every day Alma reads your sessions in raw/ and rewrites the wiki pages they touch, with sources. For anyone whose work compounds and is shared with others.

Batteries included. Run brain init and you get the loop out of the box: daily capture, self-updating wiki, evals, doctor and review. No glue code. For teams where priorities change every week.

## How it works

One brain for many agents: every agent searches the same memory, and changes come as pull requests you approve.

A brain is a folder. Instructions are AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, and skills/ (symlinked per tool). Notes, chats, and imports land in 01-raw/. Alma writes 02-wiki/ from them, with sources. 03-system/ holds jobs, evals, and logs. teambrain.yaml runs the nightly jobs.

Checked knowledge and principles live in 02-wiki/. Agents search that wiki (hybrid semantic and keyword search, over MCP) and propose updates as pull requests. Claude Code hooks can bring matches into a session.

Alma is the interface: that folder, teambrain.yaml, the brain commands, the hooks, and MCP search. Your brain is the class — your config and your content.

class MyBrain implements SecondBrain

Your content stays in your own git repo. Agents propose changes as pull requests you review. Plain markdown, no lock-in.

## Commands

The command name is still `brain` for now.

brain init <path> — Create a brain at that path and ask which sources to import.
brain doctor — Check the setup. For each problem, one line on how to fix it.
brain ask — Ask a question. The answer comes from your notes and links the source.
brain index — Rebuild the search index from the markdown in this brain.
brain query — Search the brain and print the matches.
brain retro — Review recent agent sessions and propose updates.
brain lint — Report stale docs, idle folders, duplicates, and broken links. Read-only.
brain review — Show one stale or disputed item at a time: keep, fix, or archive. Never a wall.
brain snapshot — Save local-only history for a working folder the brain's git ignores.
brain schedule — Run a brain command on a timer.
brain onboard — Connect an agent in this folder so it can search the brain.
brain wip — List notes and proposals still outside the wiki.
brain suggest — Draft a proposed update for you to review.

## Quickstart

From clone to first answer on your own notes in under 10 minutes.

git clone https://github.com/ohsuvorav/alma-brain.git
cd alma-brain
brain setup
brain init my-brain
brain doctor

brain init asks which sources to import: a markdown or Obsidian folder, Notion or Google Docs via MCP, or Claude memory and chat exports.

Then ask your agent a question. It answers from your notes, with a link to the source.

Or tell your coding agent: Install Alma by following https://github.com/ohsuvorav/alma-brain/blob/main/INSTALL.md

The repository is not public yet.

## First 10 minutes

Install, import, first answer, then one review card. The pictures on the site are a static illustration of those screens. They are not real data.
